grid_sizes_decisive_numbers.triangulated_conclusion: Three independently-generated DPW-7 grid families for the same CRM wing-body(-tail) geometry, plus DPW-8's own directly-measured Level-3 grid, all agree: the coarsest ('Tiny'/Level-1) member of any credible grid family for this geometry lands in the 5-31 million cell/point range, with the unstructured families (the ones most comparable to our own OpenFOAM/snappyHexMesh pipeline) clustering at 8-12 million. This is not a workshop-arbitrary number -- it is set by the CRM's own geometric complexity plus the gridding guidelines' wall-spacing/farfield requirements (y+~1 at Re=5e6-30e6, farfield >100 chords).

methodology_transferable_regardless_of_p: Explicit, formulaic 6-member grid-family growth rule keyed to a 'Level' index ([(L+2)/(L+1)]^3 per level), not ad hoc refinement -- enables proper Richardson extrapolation / GCI across the whole family, not just dual-mesh comparison.

y+-anchored wall-normal spacing tables pre-computed for two Reynolds-number regimes (5e6 and 30e6), with an explicit growth-rate ceiling (<1.2x normal to walls) and a minimum-2-constant-spacing-cells-at-the-wall rule -- directly reusable in our own snappyHexMesh/pyHyp layer specs on any future case, independent of whether we ever touch a DPW grid.

Fully-qualified turbulence-model naming as a documented scatter-reduction lever: 'French Vanilla SA-(neg) (All-terms)' is a specific SA variant, not generic 'SA' -- the workshop's own history (Source of Scatter WG) treats ambiguous turbulence-model specification as a measured source of code-to-code disagreement.

Convergence discipline to ~1e-10 (machine precision) for the scatter-reduction case, a bar roughly 10^4-10^5x tighter than our production standard of 1e-5/1e-6 -- worth treating as an aspirational ceiling for our own doctrine, not something to match on every case.

Standardized force/moment, surface-cut, spanload, and bending/twist submission templates in a common Tecplot ASCII schema -- the DPW convention of decomposing pressure vs. friction drag and reporting participant scatter as an explicit IQR/std band (captured for DPW-VI in docs/DPW-CRM-SCOPING.md: IQR 252-262 counts) is the field's state of the art for honestly quantifying code-to-code disagreement, and is directly transferable to how this lab reports its own campaign uncertainty.

The 'drag increment vs. absolute drag' distinction (increments scatter ~3x less than absolute values) -- already captured in the prior scoping report, reconfirmed here as still the field's cheapest path to a credible number if absolute-drag precision is out of reach.

hardware_baseline.largest_converged_primal: 579,072 cells (CRM_Wing, wing-alone, DAFoam tutorial CD match to 0.0067%), 16 vCPU / 32 GiB host, 431s wall / 28.7 core-min for 1000 SIMPLE iterations to 1e-8 residual on every field
hardware_baseline.adjoint_memory_wall: works at 63,920 cells; Jacobian-assembly OOM at 156,089 cells; also OOMs at 399,360 cells under both 12GB and 18GB container caps -- the wall sits somewhere in [63,920, 156,089] cells and is structural (OpenMDAO's reverse-mode sweep builds a mesh-sized d[residuals]/d[vol_coords] Jacobian block regardless of which wrt= is requested), not simply memory-cap-tunable
hardware_baseline.corroborating_evidence: DAFoam's own DPW4_Aircraft tutorial (the actual wing-body-tail case) was independently rejected on time-box grounds because it ships snappyHexMesh refinement levels 9-12, a 200,000,000-cell cap, and 192-rank decomposeParDict -- i.e. the tutorial vendor itself assumes HPC scale for a true CRM wing-body-tail case

per_case_verdicts.case: Config B/C/D CRM Wing/Body(-Tail)(-Nacelle-Pylon), Test Cases 2a/2b/3b/4a/4b (the DPW-8 headline drag cases) and HAWG flutter case
per_case_verdicts.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE on this hardware at any offered grid level
per_case_verdicts.reasoning: coarsest available grid in this geometry's lineage is ~11.6M cells (DPW-8, derived) to 5.3-31.6M cells (DPW-7, three independent providers, directly measured). That is 9x-55x our largest-ever converged primal (579,072 cells) and 75x-495x our adjoint's already-failing threshold (156,089 cells). The workshop's own 6-grid Richardson requirement and 1e-10 convergence bar multiply the effective cost several-fold beyond a single solve at the coarsest level.

per_case_verdicts.verdict: GEOMETRICALLY SMALLER, GATED BY MISSING CAPABILITY -- not a size problem, a capability problem
per_case_verdicts.reasoning: no published grid-size figures found, but a 130mm x 80mm cantilever plate and a clamped panel are 2-3 orders of magnitude smaller in domain extent than a full CRM aircraft. This lab has demonstrated supersonic rhoCentralFoam accuracy (<1% vs exact theory on wedge/cone/diamond, F3 campaign) but has NOT stood up a structural/FSI solver for panel flutter -- a different, currently-missing capability, not a mesh-size wall.

what_a_bigger_machine_would_need.primal_only_at_coarsest_CRM_grid: roughly 20x our current largest converged case (11.6M vs 579,072 cells). Our 32 GiB host was NOT memory-bound at 579,072 cells (30GB free throughout the A6 run) -- if primal RAM scales close to linearly with cell count (unlike the adjoint, which is structurally worse), the coarsest CRM grid might fit in well under 32GB IF partitioned across substantially more ranks than our current 4-16-vCPU ceiling allows for sane wall-time -- DAFoam's own DPW4_Aircraft tutorial defaults to 192 ranks for exactly this reason. This is a compute/rank-count problem more than a hard memory wall, for the primal alone.
what_a_bigger_machine_would_need.adjoint_at_any_CRM_scale: categorically out of reach by adding RAM alone -- A3/A6's own finding is that the OOM is structural (an unavoidable mesh-sized Jacobian block in OpenMDAO's reverse-mode sweep), not simply memory-cap-tunable. Would need either a genuinely much larger dedicated-RAM host with empirically-measured peak RSS on a small case first, or an untested matrix-free adjoint path (adjUseColoring=False) that trades memory for an unknown runtime cost.
what_a_bigger_machine_would_need.full_6-grid_Richardson_family_to_Level_6: hundreds of millions of cells at the finest level (221M-368M cells/points across the three DPW-7 families measured) -- squarely multi-node HPC-cluster territory, not a single-box upgrade. This matches the prior scoping report's independent DPW-VI estimate (7.2M-714M cell family) almost exactly, unsurprising since DPW-8 continues the DPW-7 geometry lineage.

feasibility_verdict.coarsest_feasible_entry: NONE identified among the DPW-8/AePW-4 CRM-scale cases (Configs A-D, HAWG) at any grid level offered -- every measured or derived 'Tiny'/Level-1 grid for this geometry, across four independent providers spanning DPW-7 and DPW-8, is 9x or more beyond our largest-ever converged case. The 2D verification cases (V1/V2/V3) remain an open, unconfirmed possibility pending a cheap next step (unzip and count), not a settled feasible entry.

recommendation.do_not: attempt any DPW-8/AePW-4 CRM-configuration (Config A/B/C/D) or HAWG submission on current hardware -- every measured coarsest grid is far beyond what this lab has ever converged, and the adjoint fails at a fraction of even that coarsest number.
do: download and unzip the OAT15A (V1) grid bundles (already located, ~284MB unstructured / ~554MB structured, anonymous HTTP, no compute cost) and count actual per-level cells before committing to anything further -- this is the one open question standing between 'not feasible' and 'plausible' for this workshop family.

if V1/V2/V3 cell counts land inside our proven envelope (order 10^4-10^6), consider an OFF-CYCLE, NON-SUBMITTED validation run reusing our proven F2-campaign transonic pipeline (rhoCentralFoam/kOmegaSST) against DPW-8's own committee-supplied OAT15A grid, purely to cross-check our own numbers against a workshop-standard grid -- not as a workshop submission (the June 2026 event has already passed).

bank the transferable methodology (grid-family growth formula, y+-anchored spacing tables, fully-qualified turbulence-model naming, IQR/std scatter reporting, drag-increment-vs-absolute distinction) into our own doctrine regardless of whether we ever touch DPW/AePW data directly.

treat the FEM/structural data (NASA_CRM_FULLSPAN_WBT0, NASA_CRM_HALFSPAN_FEM, both openly downloadable) as a possible future resource if this lab ever stands up a structural/FSI solver -- not actionable today, since we have no aeroelastic coupling capability.
